canary.verdict: A NuGet package named MMP.Herald.Compat.Serilog (DLL MMP.Herald.Compat.Serilog.dll) that ships the namespace Serilog.* surface compiles and runs 'using Serilog;' code with ZERO source change and no file collision. honest-claim 5 is incorrect as written. The one true constraint (CS0433 when real Serilog coexists) holds and is the expected cutover rule.

projects.title: Worker / Console
projects.serilogShape: Log.* + Console/File sinks + appsettings.json via ReadFrom.Configuration
projects.notes: Config-driven app. Not zero-source-change-eligible (no Layer-2 ReadFrom.Configuration bridge). Find-replace is the realistic vehicle. Program.cs: using Serilog -> using MMP.Herald.Serilog, plus an ADDED using Herald.OSS.Serilog.Settings (ReadFrom.Configuration lives there). csproj swaps Serilog* sink packages for MMP.Herald.Serilog + Herald.OSS.Serilog.Settings. Output is semantically identical at the level/message layer, but the rendered FORMAT differs (console template, UTC/ISO timestamp, numeric level suffix, DateTimeOffset culture) — log-scraping regexes tuned to Serilog's default text format would need updating.
gotchas: ReadFrom.Configuration requires an ADDED 'using Herald.OSS.Serilog.Settings;' — it is NOT a single-line namespace swap for config-driven apps. The extension hangs off the Herald.OSS.Serilog.Settings namespace, not Serilog/MMP.Herald.Serilog.

projects.title: ASP.NET Core Minimal API
projects.notes: ASP.NET case. UseSerilog and UseSerilogRequestLogging carry over (extensions sit in the framework namespaces the app already imports). Request-logging middleware fires (verified: 'HTTP GET / responded 200'). Two small parity adjustments required: CreateBootstrapLogger() -> CreateLogger(); CloseAndFlushAsync() -> CloseAndFlush(). Plus the same added using Herald.OSS.Serilog.Settings for ReadFrom.Configuration.
gotchas: LoggerConfiguration.CreateBootstrapLogger() is not in the Herald surface. Use CreateLogger().
Log.CloseAndFlushAsync() is not in the Herald surface. Use the sync CloseAndFlush().
ReadFrom.Configuration needs the added using Herald.OSS.Serilog.Settings; (same as Ref1).

projects.title: Custom Sink + Custom Enricher (extension author)
projects.serilogShape: ILogEventSink + ILogEventEnricher, inline-wired (WriteTo.Sink / Enrich.With), no config
projects.notes: FLAGSHIP zero-source-change result. Program.cs is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the real-Serilog baseline (custom ILogEventSink + ILogEventEnricher keep using Serilog.Core/Serilog.Events). Only the csproj changed: PackageReference Serilog -> MMP.Herald.Compat.Serilog (the renamed canary package). Custom sink fires, counts 4 events, enricher runs. Proves an extension-author app migrates with NO source edits via the renamed package.
gotchas: Herald RenderMessage() does not quote string values (init vs "init") — a rendered-text difference, not a semantic/behavior change.
Requires the renamed package MMP.Herald.Compat.Serilog (built this run); it is not yet a published vehicle. Today's shipped MMP.Herald.Serilog would need the find-replace instead.

projects.title: Destructuring Policy + Serilog.Expressions Filter
projects.serilogShape: Destructure.ByTransforming<T> redaction + Filter.ByExcluding(string) expression DSL, inline
projects.notes: Advanced case. Two real boundaries surfaced. (1) LoggerConfiguration has NO .Filter property, so the fluent .Filter.ByExcluding("...") call site does not compile; the expressions string-DSL engine ships (Filter.ByExcluding(string) -> ILogFilter, contradicting the stale expressions-dsl.md hard-wall claim) but is not wired as a LoggerConfiguration.Filter fluent step. The /health line is NOT dropped after migration. (2) SECURITY: Destructure.ByTransforming redaction is BYPASSED on native sinks (WriteTo.Console) — the ApiKey secret LEAKS. Migrated build succeeds but runtime behavior diverges from baseline, so migrated.runs is marked false (does not faithfully reproduce the app).
gotchas: HIGH/SECURITY: destructuring redaction silently no-ops on native sinks (WriteTo.Console/File). Policy only fires on the WriteTo.Sink(custom) mirror path. Secret leaks. See FINDING-destructure-native-sink-leak.md + regression test REG-SERILOG-DESTRUCTURE-NATIVE-SINK.

LoggerConfiguration.Filter fluent integration is missing. The Serilog.Expressions string-DSL engine exists (Filter.ByExcluding/ByIncludingOnly take a string), but there is no .Filter.ByExcluding(...) on the config chain to apply it inline.
expressions-dsl.md is STALE: it claims the string-DSL is a hard wall, but the engine is now implemented. The real gap is the fluent LoggerConfiguration.Filter integration, not the DSL parser.
